question.text: An MFN (Most Favoured Nation) provision in an AIF side letter typically entitles an investor to:

answer.text: Receive automatic exemption from all capital calls during market downturns
A guaranteed minimum IRR of 12% p.a. regardless of fund performance
Vote as if holding 2x their economic interest on all governance matters
Elect the benefit of rights contained in OTHER investors' side letters, and potentially also the right to view those other side letters

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.1 (Role of Fund Governance) and the side-letter chapter, an MFN provision entitles an investor to elect the benefit of rights contained in other investors' side letters, and potentially also the right to view those other side letters. The side-letter chapter frames the MFN as protection against being placed in a worse position than other investors. The Trap: MFN does not grant capital-call exemptions, voting multipliers, or a guaranteed IRR — those would be economic side-rights inconsistent with the MFN concept described in the source. Note: The keyed feature is the right to elect benefits from other investors' side letters, with potential viewing rights as described in the workbook.
